title: Yitro: named for an outsider
hook: the portion with the Ten Words is named for Jethro, a Midianite priest

segments.voice: Yesterday Amalek attacked, and Aaron and Hur held up Moses' tired arms. Your line was hold up the hands. Today, a new portion, and a visitor.

A trivia question. Which portion of the Torah holds the Ten Commandments, the moment at Mount Sinai, thunder, smoke, the voice of God? And what's it called? Not Moses. Not Sinai. Not the Ten Words. It's named after Moses' father-in-law, a priest of Midian, who wasn't an Israelite at all. His name was Jethro; in Hebrew, Yitro. And before Sinai even comes into view, he walks into the camp and tells Moses he's doing his job wrong.
screen: `WHERE ARE THE TEN COMMANDMENTS?` → `NAMED FOR A PRIEST OF MIDIAN.` → `YITRO WALKS IN.`

segments.voice: Yitro has heard everything God did for Israel, and he comes to the wilderness bringing Moses' wife Zipporah and their two sons. Moses tells him the whole story, and Yitro rejoices, and blesses the God who rescued them. The next morning he watches Moses sit as judge for the people, from morning until evening, everyone lining up with their disputes. And he says, in the old Jewish translation: "The thing that thou doest is not good." You'll wear yourself out, and the people too. Then a plan. Find capable, honest, God-fearing people. Make them judges over thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens. Let them handle the small cases and bring you the great ones. And Moses listens; he does what his father-in-law says. In the Torah's telling, Israel's courts are built on the advice of an outsider. Rashi, quoting the old midrash, says Yitro had seven names, and one of them, Yeter, means addition, because he added a section to the Torah. The rabbis even argued about the timing: did he come before Sinai, or after, with the Torah moving his story here? They didn't settle it. But there it sits, right before the Ten Words, and the portion carries his name. A tradition that names the portion of Sinai after a Midianite priest is saying something about where wisdom can come from.
screen: `YITRO REJOICES AND BLESSES.` · `THE THING THAT THOU DOEST IS NOT GOOD.` · `JUDGES OF THOUSANDS TO TENS.` · `MOSES LISTENS.` · then, large: `WISDOM FROM OUTSIDE.`

segments.voice: Think of someone outside your usual circle: a different generation, background, field or faith. Picture them watching you work from morning to evening, the way Yitro watched Moses, and ask what they might notice that you can't. Let the answer surprise you if it wants to.
Yitro. Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, priest of Midian, whose advice shaped Israel's courts and whose name is on the portion of the Ten Words.
Your line: wisdom from outside. A week of walking now: the sign on the hand, the long way, the bones, the sea, Marah, the held-up hands. That's day three hundred forty-three.

howItsDone: Yitro is read in synagogue in winter; when the Ten Commandments are chanted, people in some congregations stand. Jewish teachers point out that the portion is named for Jethro, a Midianite priest.

chat.says: Why is the Ten Commandments portion named after Moses' father-in-law?
options: He was a Midianite priest whose advice shaped Israel's courts: wisdom from outside.
He wrote down the Ten Commandments for Moses, so the portion bears his name.
He carried the tablets down from the mountain when Moses grew tired.
chat.meaning: Yitro, a priest of Midian, told Moses to share the judging, and Moses listened. Naming Sinai's portion for him says something about where wisdom comes from.

notes: Exodus 18:17 quoted from JPS 1917 from memory (KJV identical in wording); verify.
